## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-trajectory-and-pseudotime-analysis-using-monocle-3/>

Part 1 of 3. Trajectory (pseudotime) analysis orders cells along continuous
transitions between cell states. Starting from the annotated Seurat object from
tutorial 4, this notebook:

1. downsamples each cell type to keep the Monocle 3 steps tractable (rare cell
   types excluded);
2. converts the Seurat object to a Monocle 3 `cell_data_set` (CDS) with
   SeuratWrappers;
3. runs `preprocess_cds()` (normalization + PCA);
4. copies the Seurat UMAP coordinates into the CDS, so that the trajectory is
   drawn on the same embedding used in earlier tutorials.

Part 2 learns the trajectory graph and orders cells; part 3 interprets the result.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 1-7). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)
library(SeuratWrappers)

# Trajectory inference
library(monocle3)

# Data manipulation and visualization
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_7_trajectory_monocle3/tut7_trajectory_monocle3_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots", "plots/trajectories", "plots/pseudotime",
            "plots/genes_over_pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names, condition levels and colors from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))
```

## Understanding the Monocle 3 workflow

Seurat object -> downsample -> `cell_data_set` -> `preprocess_cds()` ->
UMAP alignment (part 1) -> `cluster_cells()` -> `learn_graph()` ->
`order_cells()` (part 2) -> interpretation and trajectory genes (part 3).

## Load annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4

```{r step2_load_obj}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Load annotated Seurat object from Part 4
#-----------------------------------------------

# Load the complete annotated object
annotated.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$annot.subdir, params$annotated.rds)
cat("Reading in annotated Seurat object:", annotated.file, "\n")
seurat_full <- readRDS(annotated.file)

stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, sample.col, condition.col) %in% colnames(seurat_full@meta.data)))

# Verify data structure
cat("Original dataset:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(seurat_full), "\n")
cat("  Total genes:", nrow(seurat_full), "\n")
cat("  Samples:", length(unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[sample.col]])), "\n")
cat("  Cell types:", length(unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])), "\n\n")

# Check cell type distribution
cat("Cell type distribution (full dataset):\n")
cell_type_counts <- table(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
print(cell_type_counts)
cat("\n")
```

## Strategic downsampling: maintaining biological diversity

Sampling a fixed fraction from every cell type keeps all cell types represented
(unlike sampling at random from the whole dataset, which can lose rare types)
while reducing the computation required by Monocle 3.

```{r step3_downsample}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Downsample to a fraction of cells per cell type (exclude rare types)
#-----------------------------------------------

# Set seed for reproducible downsampling
set.seed(params$seed)

# Get unique cell types and exclude rare cell types (Platelets in the article;
# too rare for trajectory analysis)
all_cell_types <- unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
cell_types <- all_cell_types[!all_cell_types %in% unlist(params$exclude.celltypes)]

cat("Cell types to analyze (excluding ", paste(unlist(params$exclude.celltypes), collapse = ", "), "):\n", sep = "")
print(cell_types)
cat("\n")

# Sample a fraction from each cell type
downsampled_cells <- c()

for (cell_type in cell_types) {
  # Get cells of this type
  cells_of_type <- colnames(seurat_full)[seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]] == cell_type]

  # Calculate fraction (with a minimum number of cells for rare types)
  n_sample <- max(params$downsample.min_cells, round(length(cells_of_type) * params$downsample.fraction))

  # Don't sample more cells than exist
  n_sample <- min(n_sample, length(cells_of_type))

  # Random sample
  sampled <- sample(cells_of_type, n_sample)
  downsampled_cells <- c(downsampled_cells, sampled)

  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d → %d cells (%.1f%%)\n",
              cell_type, length(cells_of_type), n_sample,
              100 * n_sample / length(cells_of_type)))
}

# Create downsampled Seurat object
seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_full, cells = downsampled_cells)

cat("\n")
cat("Downsampled dataset:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(seurat_subset), "\n")
cat("  Cell types retained:", length(unique(seurat_subset@meta.data[[celltype.col]])), "\n")
cat("  Reduction from full dataset:",
    round(100 * (1 - ncol(seurat_subset)/ncol(seurat_full)), 1), "%\n")

# Verify cell type representation
cat("\nCell type distribution (downsampled):\n")
print(table(seurat_subset@meta.data[[celltype.col]]))
```

## Visualize the downsampled dataset

```{r step4_overview, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Visualize downsampled data
#-----------------------------------------------

# Check which UMAP is available (from Part 3 integration)
available_reductions <- names(seurat_subset@reductions)
umap_reduction <- intersect(unlist(params$umap.priority), available_reductions)[1]
if (is.na(umap_reduction)) stop("None of params$umap.priority found in object reductions: ",
                                paste(available_reductions, collapse = ", "))

cat("Using UMAP reduction:", umap_reduction, "\n\n")

# Create multi-panel overview
p1 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = celltype.col, label = TRUE,
              label.size = 3.5, pt.size = 0.8, repel = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Cell Types (Downsampled Data)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")

p2 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = condition.col, pt.size = 0.8) +
  ggtitle("Condition Distribution") +
  scale_color_manual(values = condition.colors) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

p3 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = sample.col, pt.size = 0.8) +
  ggtitle("Sample Distribution") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

# Combine plots
p_overview <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | plot_spacer())
print(p_overview)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/01_downsampled_data_overview.png"), p_overview,
       width = 16, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

cat("Saved: plots/01_downsampled_data_overview.png\n")
```

## Convert the Seurat object to a Monocle 3 CDS

```{r step5_convert_cds}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Convert Seurat to Monocle 3 CDS object using SeuratWrappers
#-----------------------------------------------

# Convert Seurat object to cell_data_set
# This automatically transfers counts, metadata, and reductions
cds <- as.cell_data_set(seurat_subset)

cat("Created Monocle 3 cell_data_set using SeuratWrappers:\n")
cat("  Cells:", ncol(cds), "\n")
cat("  Genes:", nrow(cds), "\n")
cat("  Cell metadata columns:", ncol(colData(cds)), "\n\n")

# Monocle 3's plot_cells() requires this for gene plotting
# Add gene names to rowData
rowData(cds)$gene_short_name <- rownames(cds)

cat("Fixed gene names for Monocle 3 compatibility\n")
cat("  Gene names set:", "gene_short_name" %in% colnames(rowData(cds)), "\n")
cat("  First 5 genes:", head(rowData(cds)$gene_short_name, 5), "\n\n")

# Verify what was transferred
cat("Verifying transferred information:\n")
cat("  Expression data: counts layer =",
    !is.null(counts(cds)), "\n")
cat("  Cell metadata: ", celltype.col, " =",
    celltype.col %in% colnames(colData(cds)), "\n")
cat("  Gene names: gene_short_name =",
    "gene_short_name" %in% colnames(rowData(cds)), "\n")
```

The CDS object structure (from SingleCellExperiment):

- assays: expression matrices (counts, logcounts, etc.)
- colData: cell metadata (cell types, conditions, etc.)
- rowData: gene metadata (gene names, IDs, etc.)
- reducedDims: dimensionality reductions (PCA, UMAP, etc.)

The article also shows a manual construction of the CDS, which it does not use
(`eval = FALSE` here):

```{r step5b_manual_cds, eval = FALSE}
# Manual approach (optional - not used in this tutorial)
counts_matrix <- GetAssayData(seurat_subset, layer = "counts")
cell_metadata <- seurat_subset@meta.data
gene_metadata <- data.frame(
  gene_short_name = rownames(seurat_subset),  # ← Explicitly sets gene_short_name
  row.names = rownames(seurat_subset)
)

cds_manual <- new_cell_data_set(
  expression_data = counts_matrix,
  cell_metadata = cell_metadata,
  gene_metadata = gene_metadata
)
```

## Preprocessing: normalization and dimensionality reduction

```{r step6_preprocess}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: Preprocess data (normalization and PCA)
#-----------------------------------------------

# Normalize and reduce dimensions
cds <- preprocess_cds(
  cds,
  num_dim = params$pp.num_dim,       # Number of PCA dimensions (same as Seurat)
  norm_method = params$pp.norm_method, # Log-normalization (matching Seurat)
  use_genes = NULL,                  # Use all genes (can specify variable features)
  scaling = params$pp.scaling,       # Scale genes (mean = 0, variance = 1)
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Align to the original Seurat UMAP coordinates

```{r step7_umap_align}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: Verify/transfer original UMAP coordinates to CDS
#-----------------------------------------------

# Check if SeuratWrappers already transferred UMAP
existing_reductions <- names(reducedDims(cds))
cat("Reductions in CDS after SeuratWrappers conversion:\n")
print(existing_reductions)
cat("\n")

# SeuratWrappers should have transferred UMAP, but let's verify and ensure
# it's named correctly for Monocle 3

# Get the UMAP from Seurat object (our original high-quality UMAP)
umap_coords <- seurat_subset@reductions[[umap_reduction]]@cell.embeddings

# Verify dimensions match
cat("UMAP coordinates dimension:", dim(umap_coords), "\n")
cat("Expected (cells, 2):", c(ncol(cds), 2), "\n\n")

# Add/overwrite UMAP in CDS object
# Monocle 3 expects reducedDims to be named "UMAP" for visualization
reducedDims(cds)[["UMAP"]] <- umap_coords

cat("UMAP coordinates set in CDS object\n")
cat("Available reductions:", names(reducedDims(cds)), "\n")
```
